payload: Andrew (with co-host Adam) counts down the week's ten hottest GitHub repos, ranging from an Anthropic-vetted Claude plugins collection to a self-hosted net-worth tracker. Themes throughout: run tools locally, avoid bloated vendor software, and stack free AI tiers.

points.label: Anthropic Claude plugins community
points.detail: 2,000+ security-scanned plugins condensed into one repo so an AI (Claude Code / Claude 'Co-work') can search them fast; hosts warn plugins run real code and can be as dangerous as installing any app.

points.label: awesome-gpt-image-2
points.detail: A collection of image-generation prompts (like sharing 'source code' for an image) so you can copy a prompt, tweak sections, and reproduce a similar result; includes charts and infographics.

points.label: Omarchy (heard as 'Umachi')
points.detail: DHH's (Basecamp / Ruby on Rails) Linux setup that aims to make Linux as seamless as Mac; pitched for reviving old machines Apple no longer supports; DHH said funding is now $10M.

points.label: Open Logi (open-source Logitech tool)
points.detail: Community tool to drive Logitech mice/peripherals without Logitech's bloated, login-required software; also raised because Logitech is criticized for sending data home.

points.label: OpenAI Codex
points.detail: The Codex CLI is open source and free to download, edit, and rebrand (unlike Claude Code); a tinkerer can swap in cheaper models while keeping OpenAI's interface and redistribute it.

points.label: Apache AI agent workspace
points.detail: Apache Foundation is incubating a desktop app for running local AI agents where every model call, tool call, and permission is written to an append-only log; valued as durable infrastructure though still early/beta.

points.label: Mojo
points.detail: A newer language (repeat from last week) offering Python-like flexibility with C/C++-level performance, aimed at the AI era and throwaway LLM-generated code; traction is strong but longevity uncertain.

points.label: MoneyPrinterTurbo
points.detail: Open-source video creator (described as 'CapCut but open source, no upsells') that generates video fully with AI or by combining existing video/audio and stock B-roll.

points.label: Stack of 34 free AI tiers
points.detail: Collects 34 providers' free tiers so you rotate across them as tokens run out (OpenAI to DeepSeek to Kimi, etc.); may violate some ToS; a $19/year plan sells the up-to-date list of which still work.

points.label: Sekuro (self-hosted net-worth tracker)
points.detail: Runs on your own server (Mac/Linux/Windows), connects to 2,000+ banks via SimpleFin ($1.50/mo or $15/yr), keeps finance data local, and lets you ask your AI questions QuickBooks won't allow.

notes: Sponsored by Zapier ('Zappier AI'), pitched mid-list: their MCP gives agents safe access to 8,000+ tools, and the Zapier SDK lets your users connect your software to their own apps.
Host Andrew is moving to Mexico for a year and defers the audience 'star charts / submissions' segment to next week.
Recurring editorial slant: prefer local, self-hosted, un-bloated, non-upselling open-source tools over vendor apps that phone home.
gaps: Three repo names are mangled in the machine transcript and repaired from context: item 3 'Umachi' is DHH's Omarchy, item 4 'Open Logi', and item 10 'Sekuro' — spellings not confirmable from the transcript alone.
The Zapier segment is a paid sponsor placement inserted into the countdown between items 3 and 4, not one of the ten repos.
Intro teases 'tons of free coding agents' and software to revive old computers; these resolve to the item-9 free-tier stack and item-3 Omarchy respectively, with no separate payoff.
